Computer science.fact: == History == The earliest foundations of what would become computer science predate the invention of the modern digital computer.  Machines for calculating fixed numerical tasks such as the abacus have existed since antiquity, aiding in computations such as multiplication and division.  Algorithms for performing computations have existed since antiquity, even before the development of sophisticated computing equipment.  Wilhelm Schickard designed and constructed the first working mechanical calculator in 1623.  In 1673, Gottfried Leibniz demonstrated a digital mechanical calculator, called the Stepped Reckoner.  Leibniz may be considered the first computer scientist and information theorist, because of various reasons, including the fact that he documented the binary number system, although Thomas Harriot had already done so decades earlier.  In 1820, Thomas de Colmar launched the mechanical calculator industry when he invented his simplified arithmometer, the first calculating machine strong enough and reliable enough to be used daily in an office environment

Digital camera.fact: This method uses a single sensor chip with a Bayer filter and physically moves the sensor on the focus plane of the lens to construct a higher resolution image than the native resolution of the chip. A third version combines these two methods without a Bayer filter on the chip.

Digital camera.subject: Computer & IT
Digital camera.question: A third version combines these two methods without a _____ filter on the chip
Digital camera.fact: This method uses a single sensor chip with a Bayer filter and physically moves the sensor on the focus plane of the lens to construct a higher resolution image than the native resolution of the chip. A third version combines these two methods without a Bayer filter on the chip.

Digital camera.subject: Computer & IT
Digital camera.question: Cameras that use a beam-splitter single-shot 3CCD approach, three-filter multi-shot approach, color co-site sampling or _____ X3 sensor do not use anti-aliasing filters, nor demosaicing
Digital camera.fact: Cameras that use a beam-splitter single-shot 3CCD approach, three-filter multi-shot approach, color co-site sampling or Foveon X3 sensor do not use anti-aliasing filters, nor demosaicing.

File archiver.subject: Computer & IT
File archiver.question: The _____ was Utility software for combining files.
File archiver.fact: A file archiver is utility software that combines files into a single archive file – or in less common cases, multiple files.

File archiver.subject: Computer & IT
File archiver.question: Multics also provided a magnetic tape archiver command, ta, which was perhaps the forerunner of the _____ command tar
File archiver.fact: Multics also provided a magnetic tape archiver command, ta, which was perhaps the forerunner of the Unix command tar. Not only does separating archiving from compressing follow the Unix philosophy—that each tool should provide a single capability, not attempt to accomplish everything with one tool—it has the following advantages: As compression technology progresses, users may use a different compression tool without having to change how they use the archiver.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: The _____ was Order of bytes in a computer word.
Endianness.fact: In computing, endianness is the order in which bytes within a word data type are transmitted over a data communication medium or addressed in computer memory, counting only byte significance compared to earliness. Endianness is primarily expressed as big-endian (BE) or little-endian (LE).

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: Cohen borrowed the terms from an absurd episode in the satirical novel Gulliver's Travels by _____
Endianness.fact: Cohen borrowed the terms from an absurd episode in the satirical novel Gulliver's Travels by Jonathan Swift.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: In the imaginary land of _____, scholars are fiercely divided by a never-ending debate over how correctly to break the shell of a boiled egg
Endianness.fact: In the imaginary land of Lilliput, scholars are fiercely divided by a never-ending debate over how correctly to break the shell of a boiled egg.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: Those who insist on breaking the big end of the shell are Big-_____, while their opponents who break the opposite end of the shell are Little-Endians
Endianness.fact: Those who insist on breaking the big end of the shell are Big-Endians, while their opponents who break the opposite end of the shell are Little-Endians.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: This behavior arises, for example, in _____ or similar techniques that involve packing characters into an integer, so that it becomes a sequence of specific characters in memory
Endianness.fact: This behavior arises, for example, in FourCC or similar techniques that involve packing characters into an integer, so that it becomes a sequence of specific characters in memory.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: For example, take the string "_____", stored in hexadecimal ASCII
Endianness.fact: For example, take the string "JOHN", stored in hexadecimal ASCII.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: BSD and _____ endian.h functions (from/to BE and LE, up to 64-bit)
Endianness.fact: BSD and Glibc endian.h functions (from/to BE and LE, up to 64-bit).

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: macOS OS_____Order.h macros (from/to BE and LE, up to 64-bit)
Endianness.fact: macOS OSByteOrder.h macros (from/to BE and LE, up to 64-bit). The std::byteswap function in C++23.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: For example, GNU Fortran and the _____ both support the non-standard CONVERT specifier when opening a file, e.g.: OPEN(unit, CONVERT='BIG_ENDIAN',...)
Endianness.fact: For example, GNU Fortran and the Intel Fortran Compiler both support the non-standard CONVERT specifier when opening a file, e.g.: OPEN(unit, CONVERT='BIG_ENDIAN',...).

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: Some big-endian processors (e.g., the IBM _____/360 and its successors) contain hardware instructions for lexicographically comparing varying-length character strings
Endianness.fact: Some big-endian processors (e.g., the IBM System/360 and its successors) contain hardware instructions for lexicographically comparing varying-length character strings. The IBM System/360 uses big-endian byte order, as do its successors System/370, ESA/390, and z/Architecture.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: The IBM _____/360 uses big-endian byte order, as do its successors System/370, ESA/390, and z/Architecture
Endianness.fact: Some big-endian processors (e.g., the IBM System/360 and its successors) contain hardware instructions for lexicographically comparing varying-length character strings. The IBM System/360 uses big-endian byte order, as do its successors System/370, ESA/390, and z/Architecture.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: The IBM _____/1 minicomputer uses big-endian byte order
Endianness.fact: The IBM Series/1 minicomputer uses big-endian byte order. The Motorola 6800 / 6801, the 6809 and the 68000 series of processors use the big-endian format.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: Solely big-endian architectures include the IBM z/_____ and OpenRISC
Endianness.fact: Solely big-endian architectures include the IBM z/Architecture and OpenRISC.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: When Intel developed the 8008 microprocessor for _____, they used little-endian for compatibility
Endianness.fact: The Datapoint 2200 used simple bit-serial logic with little-endian to facilitate carry propagation. When Intel developed the 8008 microprocessor for Datapoint, they used little-endian for compatibility.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: IBM AIX and IBM i run in big-endian mode on bi-endian Power ISA; Linux originally ran in big-endian mode, but by _____, IBM had transitioned to little-endian mode for Linux to ease the porting of Linu
Endianness.fact: IBM AIX and IBM i run in big-endian mode on bi-endian Power ISA; Linux originally ran in big-endian mode, but by 2019, IBM had transitioned to little-endian mode for Linux to ease the porting of Linux software from x86 to Power.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: SPARC has no relevant little-endian deployment, as both _____ and Linux run in big-endian mode on bi-endian SPARC systems, and can be considered big-endian in practice
Endianness.fact: SPARC has no relevant little-endian deployment, as both Oracle Solaris and Linux run in big-endian mode on bi-endian SPARC systems, and can be considered big-endian in practice.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: ARM, C-Sky, and _____-V have no relevant big-endian deployments and can be considered little-endian in practice
Endianness.fact: ARM, C-Sky, and RISC-V have no relevant big-endian deployments and can be considered little-endian in practice.

Endianness.subject: Computer & IT
Endianness.question: For instance, the BQ27421 _____ battery gauge uses the little-endian format for its registers and the big-endian format for its random-access memory
Endianness.fact: For instance, the BQ27421 Texas Instruments battery gauge uses the little-endian format for its registers and the big-endian format for its random-access memory.

File system.subject: Computer & IT
File system.question: The _____ was Computer filing system.
File system.fact: In computing, a file system or filesystem (often abbreviated to FS or fs) governs file organization and access. A local file system is a capability of an operating system that services the applications running on the same computer.

File system.subject: Computer & IT
File system.question: _____ and before the advent of computers, the terms file system, filing system and system for filing were used to describe methods of organizing, storing and retrieving paper documents
File system.fact: 1900 and before the advent of computers, the terms file system, filing system and system for filing were used to describe methods of organizing, storing and retrieving paper documents.

File system.subject: Computer & IT
File system.question: By _____, the term file system was being applied to computerized filing alongside the original meaning
File system.fact: By 1961, the term file system was being applied to computerized filing alongside the original meaning.

File system.subject: Computer & IT
File system.question: By _____, it was in general use
File system.fact: By 1964, it was in general use.

File system.subject: Computer & IT
File system.question: For example, the names _____ and myfile match the same file for case-insensitive, but different files for case-sensitive
File system.fact: For example, the names MYFILE and myfile match the same file for case-insensitive, but different files for case-sensitive.

File system.subject: Computer & IT
File system.question: For example, in _____ of the early 1980s, 256-byte sectors on 140 kilobyte floppy disk used a track/sector map
File system.fact: For example, in Apple DOS of the early 1980s, 256-byte sectors on 140 kilobyte floppy disk used a track/sector map.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: The _____ was International standards for dates and times.
ISO 8601.fact: ISO 8601 is an international standard covering the worldwide exchange and communication of date and time-related data. ISO 8601 applies to these representations and formats: dates, in the Gregorian calendar (including the proleptic Gregorian calendar); times, based on the 24-hour timekeeping system, with optional UTC offset, time intervals, and combinations thereof.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: It is maintained by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and was first published in _____, with updates in 1991, 2000, 2004, and 2019, and an amendment in 2022
ISO 8601.fact: It is maintained by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and was first published in 1988, with updates in 1991, 2000, 2004, and 2019, and an amendment in 2022.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: ISO _____: Numbering of weeks, also from April 1976 with ISO R 2015 from 1971, first specified the rules for determining the ordinal number of a calendar week in a year and a day within a week
ISO 8601.fact: ISO 2015: Numbering of weeks, also from April 1976 with ISO R 2015 from 1971, first specified the rules for determining the ordinal number of a calendar week in a year and a day within a week.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: ISO 2711: Representation of ordinal dates, issued in January _____, introduced the notation for the day of the year, which effectively treats only the final, 366th day of leap years differently
ISO 8601.fact: ISO 2711: Representation of ordinal dates, issued in January 1973, introduced the notation for the day of the year, which effectively treats only the final, 366th day of leap years differently.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: ISO 3307: Representation of time of the day, dated March _____, standardized 24-hour wall clock times and their notation, but without handling time zones
ISO 8601.fact: ISO 3307: Representation of time of the day, dated March 1975, standardized 24-hour wall clock times and their notation, but without handling time zones.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: ISO 4031: Representation of time of the day, published December _____, added numerical offsets from UTC (or GMT back then)
ISO 8601.fact: ISO 4031: Representation of time of the day, published December 1978, added numerical offsets from UTC (or GMT back then).

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: This first, unified edition was superseded by a second edition, ISO 8601:_____, in 2000, that by a revised, third edition, ISO 8601:2004, published on 1 December 2004, and that by ISO 8601-1:2019 and
ISO 8601.fact: This first, unified edition was superseded by a second edition, ISO 8601:2000, in 2000, that by a revised, third edition, ISO 8601:2004, published on 1 December 2004, and that by ISO 8601-1:2019 and ISO 8601-2:2019 on 25 February 2019.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: Issued in February _____, the fourth revision of the standard, ISO 8601-1:2019, represents slightly updated contents of the previous ISO 8601:2004 standard, but is now the first of two parts
ISO 8601.fact: This first, unified edition was superseded by a second edition, ISO 8601:2000, in 2000, that by a revised, third edition, ISO 8601:2004, published on 1 December 2004, and that by ISO 8601-1:2019 and ISO 8601-2:2019 on 25 February 2019. Issued in February 2019, the fourth revision of the standard, ISO 8601-1:2019, represents slightly updated contents of the previous ISO 8601:2004 standard, but is now the first of two parts.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: The other part, ISO 8601-2:_____, is entirely new
ISO 8601.fact: This first, unified edition was superseded by a second edition, ISO 8601:2000, in 2000, that by a revised, third edition, ISO 8601:2004, published on 1 December 2004, and that by ISO 8601-1:2019 and ISO 8601-2:2019 on 25 February 2019. Issued in February 2019, the fourth revision of the standard, ISO 8601-1:2019, represents slightly updated contents of the previous ISO 8601:2004 standard, but is now the first of two parts.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: It defines various extensions such as uncertainties or parts of the _____/Time Format (EDTF)
ISO 8601.fact: It defines various extensions such as uncertainties or parts of the Extended Date/Time Format (EDTF).

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: An amendment to ISO 8601-1 was published in October _____ featuring minor technical clarifications and attempts to remove ambiguities in definitions
ISO 8601.fact: An amendment to ISO 8601-1 was published in October 2022 featuring minor technical clarifications and attempts to remove ambiguities in definitions.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: An amendment to ISO 8601-2 was published in January _____
ISO 8601.fact: An amendment to ISO 8601-2 was published in January 2025.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: For example, the 6th day of the 1st month of the year _____ may be written as "2009-01-06" in the extended format or as "20090106" in the basic format without ambiguity
ISO 8601.fact: For example, the 6th day of the 1st month of the year 2009 may be written as "2009-01-06" in the extended format or as "20090106" in the basic format without ambiguity.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: For example, "_____-05" is a valid ISO 8601 date, which indicates May (the fifth month) 2004
ISO 8601.fact: For example, "2004-05" is a valid ISO 8601 date, which indicates May (the fifth month) 2004. This format will never represent the 5th day of an unspecified month in 2004, nor will it represent a time-span extending from 2004 into 2005.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: This format will never represent the 5th day of an unspecified month in _____, nor will it represent a time-span extending from 2004 into 2005
ISO 8601.fact: For example, "2004-05" is a valid ISO 8601 date, which indicates May (the fifth month) 2004. This format will never represent the 5th day of an unspecified month in 2004, nor will it represent a time-span extending from 2004 into 2005.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: ISO 8601 allows Gregorian dates from the introduction of the calendar on 15 October _____
ISO 8601.fact: ISO 8601 allows Gregorian dates from the introduction of the calendar on 15 October 1582.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: For earlier (pre-_____) dates, the calendar may be extended before its introduction (the proleptic Gregorian calendar) by explicit agreement of the parties involved
ISO 8601.fact: ISO 8601 allows Gregorian dates from the introduction of the calendar on 15 October 1582. For earlier (pre-Gregorian) dates, the calendar may be extended before its introduction (the proleptic Gregorian calendar) by explicit agreement of the parties involved.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: Such proleptic dates may not be adjusted to reconcile them with _____ dates
ISO 8601.fact: Such proleptic dates may not be adjusted to reconcile them with Julian dates.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: However, years before _____ (the first full year following the introduction of the Gregorian calendar) are not automatically allowed by the standard
ISO 8601.fact: However, years before 1583 (the first full year following the introduction of the Gregorian calendar) are not automatically allowed by the standard.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: For example, "5 April _____" may be represented as either "1981-04-05" in the extended format or "19810405" in the basic format
ISO 8601.fact: For example, "5 April 1981" may be represented as either "1981-04-05" in the extended format or "19810405" in the basic format. For example, one may write "1981-04" to mean "1981 April".

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: For example, one may write "_____-04" to mean "1981 April"
ISO 8601.fact: For example, "5 April 1981" may be represented as either "1981-04-05" in the extended format or "19810405" in the basic format. For example, one may write "1981-04" to mean "1981 April".

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: One may simply write "_____" to refer to that year, "198" to refer to the decade from 1980 to 1989 inclusive, or "19" to refer to the century from 1900 to 1999 inclusive
ISO 8601.fact: For example, "5 April 1981" may be represented as either "1981-04-05" in the extended format or "19810405" in the basic format. For example, one may write "1981-04" to mean "1981 April".

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: Although the standard allows both the "_____-MM-DD" and YYYYMMDD formats for complete calendar date representations, if the day [DD] is omitted then only the YYYY-MM format is allowed
ISO 8601.fact: Although the standard allows both the "YYYY-MM-DD" and YYYYMMDD formats for complete calendar date representations, if the day [DD] is omitted then only the YYYY-MM format is allowed. By disallowing dates of the form YYYYMM, the standard avoids confusion with the truncated representation YYMMDD (still often used).

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT

ISO 8601.fact: Although the standard allows both the "YYYY-MM-DD" and YYYYMMDD formats for complete calendar date representations, if the day [DD] is omitted then only the YYYY-MM format is allowed. By disallowing dates of the form YYYYMM, the standard avoids confusion with the truncated representation YYMMDD (still often used).

ISO 8601.question: The week number can be described by counting the _____: Week 12 contains the 12th Thursday of the year
ISO 8601.fact: The week number can be described by counting the Thursdays: Week 12 contains the 12th Thursday of the year.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: The ISO week-numbering year starts at the first day (_____) of week 01 and ends at the Sunday before the new ISO year (hence without overlap or gap)
ISO 8601.fact: The ISO week-numbering year starts at the first day (Monday) of week 01 and ends at the Sunday before the new ISO year (hence without overlap or gap). The first ISO week of a year may have up to three days that are actually in the Gregorian calendar year that is ending; if three, they are Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: The first ISO week of a year may have up to three days that are actually in the _____ calendar year that is ending; if three, they are Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday
ISO 8601.fact: The first ISO week of a year may have up to three days that are actually in the Gregorian calendar year that is ending; if three, they are Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. Similarly, the last ISO week of a year may have up to three days that are actually in the Gregorian calendar year that is starting; if three, they are Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: Similarly, the last ISO week of a year may have up to three days that are actually in the _____ calendar year that is starting; if three, they are Friday, Saturday, and Sunday
ISO 8601.fact: The first ISO week of a year may have up to three days that are actually in the Gregorian calendar year that is ending; if three, they are Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. Similarly, the last ISO week of a year may have up to three days that are actually in the Gregorian calendar year that is starting; if three, they are Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: The Thursday of each ISO week is always in the _____ calendar year denoted by the ISO week-numbering year
ISO 8601.fact: The first ISO week of a year may have up to three days that are actually in the Gregorian calendar year that is ending; if three, they are Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. Similarly, the last ISO week of a year may have up to three days that are actually in the Gregorian calendar year that is starting; if three, they are Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT

ISO 8601.question: For example, "_____-04-05" is the same as "1981-095"
ISO 8601.fact: For example, "1981-04-05" is the same as "1981-095".

ISO 8601.fact: As of ISO 8601-1:2019, the basic format is T[hh][mm][ss] and the extended format is T[hh]:[mm]:[ss].

ISO 8601.fact: ISO 8601-1:2019 allows the T to be omitted in the extended format, as in "13:47:30", but only allows the T to be omitted in the basic format when there is no risk of confusion with date expressions. ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT
ISO 8601.question: As of ISO 8601-1:_____/Amd 1:2022, "00:00:00" may be used to refer to midnight corresponding to the instant at the beginning of a calendar day; and "24:00:00" to refer to midnight corresponding to the
ISO 8601.fact: ISO 8601-1:2019 allows the T to be omitted in the extended format, as in "13:47:30", but only allows the T to be omitted in the basic format when there is no risk of confusion with date expressions. ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT

ISO 8601-1:2019 as originally published removed "24:00:00" as a representation for the end of day although it had been permitted in earlier versions of the standard.

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT

ISO 8601.fact: For example, in Microsoft SQL Server, the precision of a decimal fraction is 3 for a DATETIME, i.e., "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss[.mmm]".

ISO 8601.subject: Computer & IT

ISO 8601.fact: So the zone designation for New York (on standard time) would be "−05:00", "−0500", or "−05".

ISO week date.subject: Computer & IT
ISO week date.question: The _____ was Leap week calendar system.
ISO week date.fact: The ISO week date system is effectively a leap week calendar system that is part of the ISO 8601 date and time standard issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) since 1988 (last revised in 2019) and, before that, it was defined in ISO (R) 2015 since 1971.

ISO week date.subject: Computer & IT
ISO week date.question: This was previously known as "_____ date coding"
ISO week date.fact: This was previously called "Industrial date coding".

ISO week date.subject: Computer & IT
ISO week date.question: The system specifies a week year atop the _____ calendar by defining a notation for ordinal weeks of the year
ISO week date.fact: The system specifies a week year atop the Gregorian calendar by defining a notation for ordinal weeks of the year. The Gregorian leap cycle, which has 97 leap days spread across 400 years, contains a whole number of weeks (20871).

Commitment scheme.subject: Computer & IT
Commitment scheme.question: The _____ was Cryptographic scheme.
Commitment scheme.fact: A commitment scheme is a cryptographic primitive that allows one to commit to a chosen value (or chosen statement) while keeping it hidden to others, with the ability to reveal the committed value later.
